title: Low-bit fallback topology and kernel contracts (proposal)
body:
Purpose

This doc proposes a topology-first approach for low-bit execution fallback and an explicit kernel capability contract that the runtime, scheduler, and KV cache will use to interoperate across INT8, FP8, GPTQ, and AWQ variants. Goal: enable safe, automatic fallback between precision classes in-path with minimal latency impact and deterministic KV cache semantics.

Background / motivation

We have many partial implementations of quantized kernels (INT8, AWQ, GPTQ) and emerging FP8 paths. Previously we focused on per-kernel heuristics and ad-hoc compatibility flags. That approach leaks complexity into the scheduler and makes cross-model fallbacks non-deterministic. Instead, define: 1) a small set of topology profiles (how kernels are wired for a model), 2) a kernel contract surface area describing what each kernel variant guarantees, and 3) a KV cache versioning and migration plan for in-flight fallback.

Key ideas (high level)

- Topology profiles: canonical execution graphs (e.g., Embedding->Attention->FFN with KV cache) annotated with precision bands for each stage (embedding, attn_qkv, attn_out, ffn). Runtimes choose a profile that best matches hardware and latency constraints.
- Kernel contracts: capability flags + behavioral guarantees (numerical range, deterministic rounding, statelessness, portable weight layout). Kernels must surface a compact descriptor at registration.
- Fallback topology: a sequence of compatible topologies ordered by cost/latency. The scheduler may switch topologies per-request or per-connection.
- KV cache coherence: define a per-entry header with precision tag + transform function id to enable lazy on-read conversion and deterministic fallbacks.

Topology profiles (example)

1) profile-light-8: embedding=int8, attn_qkv=int8, attn_out=fp16, ffn=int8, kv-cache=int8-packed
2) profile-balanced-8f: embedding=fp8, attn_qkv=int8, attn_out=fp8, ffn=fp8, kv-cache=fp8-blocked
3) profile-fp16-compat: embedding=fp16, attn_qkv=fp16, attn_out=fp16, ffn=fp16, kv-cache=fp16

Each profile includes a compatibility tag set to compare with kernel descriptors. Profiles are intentionally coarse-grained to reduce combinatorial explosion.

Kernel contract (registration descriptor)

Each kernel registers a single-line JSON descriptor at startup (runtime-facing, not user doc). Fields: kernel_id (string), precision (one of: int8, awq, gptq, fp8, fp16), layout (packed | blocked | planar), kv_support (none | read-only | read-write), deterministic (true|false), rounding (nearest|stochastic|trunc), max_seq (int), supported_batch_dims (comma-separated), weight_hash (hex). Runtime will check: profile.precision subset kernel.precision and layout match.

Example descriptor (human):
- kernel_id: conv_attn_int8_v2
- precision: int8
- layout: packed
- kv_support: read-write
- deterministic: true
- rounding: nearest
- max_seq: 4096
- supported_batch_dims: B,1
- weight_hash: ab12f3...

Compatibility check rules (simple)

1) Precision compatibility: kernel precision must be in the allowed set for the profile stage. E.g., profile allows int8 or fp8 => kernel.precision must be one of them.
2) Layout compatibility: profile specifies a layout; kernel.layout must match or runtime must have a layout adaptor path (see below).
3) KV contract: if profile requires kv read-write but kernel reports read-only, that kernel cannot be used for that profile without a KV gateway conversion layer.

KV cache versioning and on-read conversion

- KV entries include a 8-byte header: {version:1, precision_tag, transform_id, reserved}.
- On switch from profile A->B where kv formats differ, runtime will either: (a) lazily convert entries on first read (preferred for latency), or (b) trigger background bulk conversion when traffic idle.
- Transform functions are deterministic and registered in the runtime (id -> function). Transform ids are part of kernel descriptors for traceability.

Lazy conversion semantics

1) Request reading KV entry with header.precision != active_precision => call transform(transform_id, src_buf) to produce expected format then cache converted entry alongside original with new header version (copy-on-read).
2) Transforms must be idempotent and deterministic; non-deterministic transforms (e.g., stochastic quantization) are forbidden for lazy conversion.

Scheduler fallback heuristics

- Primary metric is P95 token latency; secondary is cost per token.
- Topologies are ordered in a fallback chain: e.g., profile-light-8 -> profile-balanced-8f -> profile-fp16-compat.
- If a node's kernels fail compatibility checks for a profile, the scheduler skips to the next profile.
- For in-flight requests, only allow fallback to a profile that preserves KV read semantics (read-only->read-only or read-write->read-write with available gateway).

Kernel layout adaptors (small fast shims)

- For minor layout mismatches we can provide an adaptor that transforms weight layout on load (not at runtime per token). Adaptor cost is a one-time load-time memcpy/transpose. Not allowed for KV entries.

Testing & verification matrix (engineer checklist)

- Unit tests for kernel descriptor parsing (edge cases: missing fields, unknown precision).
- Cross-precision functional tests: same seed, same prompt -> verify logits within tolerance across profile swaps.
- KV conversion tests: roundtrip conversion accuracy, idempotency, transform determinism.
- Latency smoke tests: profile swap overhead <= 3ms median for lazy conversions on GPU A100 80GB.
- Fuzzing: malformed kernel descriptors, unknown transform ids -> assert graceful failure and deterministic fallback.

Operational concerns

- Observability: emit events when fallback occurs with reason codes (compatibility-mismatch, capacity, perf-regression). Include kernel_id, profile_from, profile_to, kv_transform_id.
- Telemetry: sample per-request which profile executed and per-stage kernel_id.
- Security: weight_hash must be verified on kernel registration to prevent accidental mismatch of weight layout.

Open questions / TODOs

- How to represent hybrid layers where QKV are different precisions inside a single kernel? Proposal: kernel must expose substage precision map and runtime must only accept kernels whose substage map is subset of profile stage requirements.
- Tooling: need a small CLI to inspect kernel descriptors and simulate profile compatibility for a model artifact.
- Backcompat: deploy incremental change to kernel descriptor format (v1 -> v2) with a descriptor_version field. Plan a two-release rollout.

Migration plan (phased)

1) Implement kernel descriptor surface and registration endpoint (internal runtime API).
2) Implement basic compatibility checks in scheduler and refuse mismatched kernels (non-disruptive when not enabled).
3) Add KV header + transform registry; implement lazy on-read converters for common pairs (int8<->fp16, fp8<->fp16).
4) Enable fallback chains for canary groups; collect metrics.

Appendix: short example flow (happy path)

- Model loaded with profile-light-8; all kernels register successfully. KV header version=1 precision=int8.
- Sudden capacity pressure requires fallback to profile-balanced-8f which uses fp8 for ffn. Scheduler verifies kernels: attn kernel ok, ffn kernel available (fp8) but kv layout differs.
- Scheduler marks chain as acceptable; first request hitting new profile triggers lazy conversion for KV entries encountered; events emitted.

Notes to reviewers

- This is intentionally pragmatic: small set of profiles and a strict kernel descriptor reduces runtime complexity. We trade off some per-model tuning for predictable behavior and simpler ops.
- Feedback wanted on the KV header size (8 bytes) and whether transform registry should be pluggable per-tenant.
